head: 6e27cc37
headSubject: docs(runtimehost): correct AsyncWaitResumeE2EIT comment -- DirtiesContext did not fix the hang
summary: Attempted the prior handoff's proposed fix for the AsyncWaitResumeE2EIT hang: added @DirtiesContext (commit e9aefeca) on the hypothesis that the flow-resume scheduler's leaked non-daemon thread was blocking the forked Gradle test JVM's shutdown. Verified locally first (955 tests, only a pre-existing unrelated H2 flake failed, no hang) then pushed to main and watched the real CI job. DISPROVEN live in CI run 36662397857: the 'RuntimeHost generated-app Postgres integration tests' step still hung the full 45-minute timeout, with zero further Gradle output and no completed JUnit XML report -- identical to the pre-fix symptom. NEW evidence this run: AsyncWaitResumeE2EIT now fails FAST (~14s after the integrationTest task starts) with a concrete AssertionError at an HTTP-status assertion (expected vs actual status not recoverable -- no JUnit report was ever flushed to disk), then the whole task hangs with no further output at all until GitHub's hard kill. Corrected the now-false claim in the test's comment (commit 6e27cc37) rather than leaving a wrong 'fixed' claim in the codebase; left @DirtiesContext in place since it is harmless and still correct hygiene for the one IT class that enables the scheduler.
nextStep: The leaked-scheduler-thread hypothesis is disproven as the (sole) cause. Next session should re-diagnose from scratch using the NEW evidence: the test fails fast with an HTTP-status assertion mismatch (real Postgres-specific behavioral bug in the async wait/resume flow, in the pattern of this session's other two real Postgres transaction bugs), and THEN the whole Gradle integrationTest task hangs producing zero output and no test report -- suggesting something blocks either the JVM's own shutdown/reporting phase or a stuck DB connection/lock (e.g. the resume scheduler's poll() blocked on a connection left in a bad state by the failed request), not a simple non-daemon-thread-vs-shutdown-hook race. Since Docker is unavailable locally (no Postgres testcontainer repro) and each CI cycle costs ~45min+, the next attempt should add real diagnostics BEFORE the CI hard-timeout fires -- e.g. a shorter internal timeout on the integrationTest gradle step (~10-15min) that triggers a thread dump (jstack) and/or Postgres server-side state (pg_stat_activity, pg_locks) on the child JVM/DB before GitHub's 45-minute kill -- rather than guessing at another code fix blind. Start there.
blocked: Same as before: reproducing/diagnosing this needs either a live CI cycle (~45min/attempt, now 2 consumed on this exact hang across two sessions) or Docker for a local Postgres testcontainer run -- Docker remains unavailable on this machine.
verified: runtimehost-core local test suite (H2, gradlew test via run-runtimehost-gate.ps1) run once after applying @DirtiesContext: 955 tests, 1 failed (H2LocalBootLockCrossProcessTest, pre-existing/unrelated -- Windows page-file-too-small JVM warning right next to it, a local-machine resource flake), AsyncWaitResumeE2EIT itself did not fail or hang locally. CI run 36662397857 (commit e9aefeca) on GitHub confirmed the fix did NOT resolve the real Postgres hang -- see NEXT for the new evidence this produced.
